problem: Find the $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=\sqrt{x-2}+2$ that is closest to the point $(3,2).$
worked_solution:
Let us consider the *squared* distance $S$ between $(3,2)$ and a general point $P(x,y)$:

$$
S=(x-3)^{2}+(y-2)^{2}
$$

We require that the point $P$ lies on the curve $y=\sqrt{x-2}+2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}S(x) & =(x-3)^{2}+(y-2)^{2} \\  & =(x-3)^{2}+{(\sqrt{x-2}+2-2)}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}-6x+9+x-2 \\  & ={x}^{2}-5x+7.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the minimum distance, we take the first derivative of $S(x)$ and equate it to zero. This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(x)=2x-5 & =0 \\ 2x & =5 \\ x & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(\frac{5}{2})=2>0.$ Therefore, $x=\frac{5}{2}$ is a minimum of $S.$

So, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) is minimized when $x=\frac{5}{2}.$
